stem: According to the graph, in which year was the decrease in the number of recordings from the previous year the greatest?
stimulus: A folklore archive tracked how many oral folktale recordings it added each year from 2010 to 2017.

figure.caption: Folktale Recordings Added per Year
figure.alt: Line graph of folktale recordings added per year, 2010 to 2017, rising and falling several times.

explanation: Work out the change across each one-year segment: +15, −5, +20, −25, +15, +30, −10. The question asks only about decreases, so ignore the rises. The largest drop is 25, from 70 in 2013 to 45 in 2014. A decrease from the previous year belongs to the later year, so the answer is 2014.

common_errors.why: Took the steepest segment overall, the 30-recording rise into 2016, and missed that the question asks for a decrease.
Found the right segment but gave the year the drop started from, not the year that ended lower than the one before.
Gave the year with the lowest value instead of the year with the largest drop.

stem: According to the graph, between which two consecutive years did the number of performances change by the greatest amount, either up or down? Enter the later of the two years.
stimulus: A musicologist counted the public performances of one symphony in each year from 1900 to 1907.

figure.caption: Performances of the Symphony by Year
figure.alt: Line graph of yearly performances of a symphony from 1900 to 1907.

explanation: Find the size of each one-year change and ignore its sign: 5, 20, 5, 10, 25, 5, 5. The largest is 25, the fall from 50 in 1904 to 25 in 1905. 'Either up or down' means a fall counts, so the 20-performance rise is not the biggest change. The later year of the pair is 1905.

common_errors.why: Looked only at increases and picked the 20-performance rise into 1902, missing that a decrease also counts.
Gave the earlier year of the correct pair, or the year with the highest count, instead of the later year.
Gave the year with the lowest count instead of the year that ends the largest change.

stem: According to the graph, on which night was the hourly meteor count three times the count on night 1?

explanation: First read night 1 from the graph: 12 meteors per hour. Three times that is 36. Find 36 on the vertical axis and read across to the line. Only night 6 sits at 36, so the answer is 6.

common_errors.why: Picked the year with the lowest count instead of the first year below the threshold.

Looked for the lowest point (week 8) and took the interval that ends there, comparing endpoint values instead of the change across each interval.
Found the right segment but gave the week it ends at, not the week $w$ it starts at.

stem: The greatest increase in water level from one day to the next occurred between day $n$ and day $n + 1$. What is the value of $n$?
stimulus: A hydrologist recorded the water level at a gauge on a small creek at noon on each of 8 consecutive days. The line graph shows the results.

figure.caption: Creek Water Level at Noon
figure.alt: Line graph of creek water level in centimeters for days 1 through 8: day 1, 40; day 2, 60; day 3, 50; day 4, 90; day 5, 80; day 6, 40; day 7, 60; day 8, 70.

explanation: Read the level on each day, then find the change across each one-day segment: day 1 to 2 is +20, day 2 to 3 is −10, day 3 to 4 is +40, day 4 to 5 is −10, day 5 to 6 is −40, day 6 to 7 is +20, and day 7 to 8 is +10. The question asks for an increase, so you only look at the segments that rise. The steepest rising segment goes from day 3 to day 4, a 40-centimeter increase, so n = 3. The 40-centimeter drop from day 5 to day 6 is just as steep, but it is a decrease, so it does not count.

common_errors.why: Picked the steepest segment without checking its direction. The segment from day 5 to day 6 is the greatest decrease, a 40-centimeter drop.
Gave the day with the highest water level, which is the end of the rise, when the question asks for the start of the interval.
Compared levels to the first day instead of finding each day-to-day change, or gave the first day of the first rising segment.

stem: After reaching its maximum, the antibody concentration first fell to 40 units per milliliter at week $w$. What is the value of $w$?
stimulus: An immunology lab measured the antibody concentration in a volunteer's blood once a week, beginning on the day of a vaccination (week 0). The line graph shows the measurements.

figure.caption: Antibody Concentration After Vaccination
figure.alt: Line graph of antibody concentration in units per milliliter for weeks 0 through 6: week 0, 10; week 1, 40; week 2, 80; week 3, 70; week 4, 40; week 5, 30; week 6, 20.

explanation: First find the maximum. The highest point is 80 units per milliliter, at week 2. Then look only at the weeks after week 2 and find the first one at the height of 40: week 3 is 70 and week 4 is 40, so w = 4. Week 1 also reads 40, but it comes before the maximum, so the qualifier rules it out.

common_errors.why: Found the first week at 40 units per milliliter without applying 'after reaching its maximum.' Week 1 is on the way up.
Gave the week of the maximum instead of the week the concentration fell to 40.
Read across from the 30 gridline instead of the 40 gridline.

stem: The greatest change, in either direction, in the number of tales recorded occurred between year $t$ and year $t + 10$. What is the value of $t$?
stimulus: A folklore archive counts how many traditional tales its collectors recorded in a regional survey taken every 10 years. The line graph shows the counts for each survey from 1900 to 1960.
explanation: Every interval is 10 years wide, so you can compare the vertical size of each segment directly. The changes are 1900 to 1910, +20; 1910 to 1920, +60; 1920 to 1930, −20; 1930 to 1940, −80; 1940 to 1950, +20; 1950 to 1960, +40. 'In either direction' means you compare sizes and ignore signs. The largest is the 80-tale drop from 1930 to 1940, so t = 1930.

common_errors.why: Looked only at increases and picked the 60-tale rise from 1910 to 1920, ignoring that a decrease also counts as a change.
Gave the year at the end of the interval, the lowest point, instead of t, the year at its start.
Picked the year with the highest count, which compares the values themselves instead of the change across each interval.
